subject: Post-call recap: performance targets, streaming behavior, and regional routing
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Apr 2025 12:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: performance targets, streaming behavior, and regional routing

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the concrete asks we agreed on.

1) Core SLOs and targets (Acme asks):
   - API p95 generation latency target: <= 120 ms for batch (non-streaming) in EU region.
   - Streaming token arrival (server->client): p95 <= 90 ms per token in EU for interactive use cases (low-latency streaming).
   - Sustained throughput: 120 tokens/sec aggregate per tenant during peak for analytics pipelines (can be sharded across instances).
   - Peak concurrency: 55 simultaneous user sessions for the primary EU cluster; per-session token rate ~ 10-15 tokens/sec.

2) Regional routing & data residency:
   - Production traffic for EU users must stay within EU region (data residency requirement).
   - Failover plan: if EU capacity is exhausted, requests may fail over to EU read-only cache or degrade to a lower-cost regional model — NOT to US/APAC without explicit approval.

3) Streaming specifics we discussed:
   - You clarified usage of chunked SSE with client-side token processing; we need sample traces showing token pacing and payload sizes.
   - We recommended enabling small prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce cold-start tokens.

4) Next steps (owners & timeline):
   - Acme to share sample traffic profile + token pacing traces by EOD Thursday (Liam / SRE).
   - Redwood to produce a short SLO feasibility spreadsheet and an initial capacity proposal for EU-only tenancy by Friday EOD (Priya + Ben).
   - Technical follow-up call to review capacity numbers and routing policy w/ network team next week (tentative: Tue 14th) — Rafael to propose times.

Attachments: acme_slo_summary.xlsx (initial template), sample_workload_profile.json (example schema)

If I missed anything, flag it and I'll update. Otherwise I'll convert this to an action tracker and loop in the network team.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health SRE <sre@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Apr 2025 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets, streaming behavior, and regional routing

Priya — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming target: the 90 ms p95 is tight — that's the requirement for our clinician-facing assistant where token-by-token responsiveness is critical. If the EU cluster can't guarantee that, we need a documented fallback that preserves EU residency (e.g., queue + fast-batch response within 350 ms).
- Throughput: the 120 tokens/sec aggregate number is across all sessions in a node pool; per-node we expect to see bursts up to 900 tokens/sec for periodic analytics jobs.
- Concurrency: 55 concurrent interactive sessions is accurate; we also have a secondary EU-only analytics tenant that can spike independently.

We'll attach sample token pacing traces and an internal doc describing failover policy by Thursday. Also, do you have any early guidance on acceptable quantization artifacts? Our compliance team prefers int8 if quality stays within a 3% BLEU/ROUGE delta.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Apr 2025 07:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets, streaming behavior, and regional routing

Adding a couple of technical notes before we do the capacity calc:

- Latency is dominated by three factors: model decode per-token, network RTT (client->edge->regional-cluster), and runtime batching. For p95 <= 90 ms token arrival we need:
   * model path: sub-40 ms per token (quantization + optimized kernels),
   * edge: < 20 ms RTT within EU region to the serving cluster,
   * batching: continuous micro-batching with max added latency <= 20 ms.

- Concurrency math (rough): assume model decode 35 ms/token, 10 tokens/sec per session => ~350 ms of model work per second per session. With a node capable of ~10k tokens/sec (decoded), that maps to ~28 concurrent interactive sessions in practice. To support 55 interactive sessions we should consider 2-3 nodes in the EU pool or using concurrent model replicas with routing by session affinity.

- Streaming fallback: recommend a policy where we perform EU-local degraded-mode using a smaller model variant (same family, quantized) to keep residency. Fallback to other regions only with signed waiver.

I'll start a quick capacity workbook and attach a first-pass calc. Priya — want me to share the workbook to the HubSpot deal (linked in the thread) or keep it internal until we get the sample traces?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Acme Health SRE <sre@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Apr 2025 08:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets, streaming behavior, and regional routing

Thanks — attaching the traces and a short CSV of session concurrency over the past 30 days (see network-trace-samples.txt). A couple of implementation notes from SRE:

- Typical client RTT to our EU edge is 25-35 ms; bursty spikes to 70 ms in certain networks.
- Token sizes average 40 bytes (compressed) with peak message sizes hitting ~1.2 KB.
- We can accept degraded-mode models as long as classification/regulatory-sensitive outputs are flagged and routed through our audit pipeline.

Action: we'll provide an annotated trace showing where token pacing caused UI stalls; please map those to your proposed batching windows and we can schedule a 45-minute technical sync next Tue (14 Apr) 09:00-09:45 UTC.

— Acme SRE
